leadText:
The Emerald arc (Japanese: エメラルド編 Emerald arc), also referred to as The Sixth Chapter (Japanese: 第六章 The Sixth Chapter), is the sixth story arc of the Pokémon Adventures , consisting of four volumes. It began serialization in February 2005, and ended in October 2008.

The arc begins with focus on a named , who is sent by Professor Oak and to within seven days. On arrival at the , he ends up interfering in the opening ceremonies and gains the second challenge of clearing the seven battle facilities by defeating the Frontier Brains within that time. During this time, Emerald befriends Todd Snap and discovers that the armored villain Guile Hideout is seeking Jirachi for his own evil purposes.

During this time, Emerald befriends Todd Snap and discovers that the armored villain Guile Hideout is seeking Jirachi for his own evil purposes.

== Terminology ==
 
This arc gets its name from the core series game, Pokémon Emerald.

==Volumes==

===Chapters===
 

==Important events==
 
 
A few months have passed since the end of the .
arrives at the and crashes the opening ceremony, after which the Frontier Brains challenge him to defeat all seven facilities in seven days.

Emerald reveals that his task is to capture .
Guile Hideout appears with Jirachi in Artisan Cave. Jirachi runs away and Guile escapes.

Guile Hideout captures Jirachi.
It is revealed that the Pokédex Holders who had been petrified at the end of the previous arc have been brought to the Battle Frontier. 
Guile Hideout's identity is revealed, and Jirachi grants his wish. A -shaped creature appears by the Battle Frontier.

Emerald's past is revealed.

The monster Kyogre is destroyed by the ten Pokédex Holders.
The mystery behind Archie's armor and sword is revealed, after which he disappears.
Emerald achieves his goals.
Jirachi returns to sleep.
Professor Oak and Crystal call Professor Rowan.

===Additions===

===Evolutions===
The following Pokémon evolve:

==Battle Frontier facility challenges==
Emerald defeats the following Frontier Brains:
Noland (PS307)
Lucy (PS310)
Brandon (PS313)
Greta (PS318)
Spenser (PS327)
Anabel (PS337)
Tucker (PS337)

==Trivia==
When this arc was being published in the magazines, it was known as the Battle Frontier arc (Japanese: バトルフロンティア編 Battle Frontier chapter). At the time, this arc was the only arc of Pokémon Adventures not named after a game.
